title: One action bar for stories and enablers
prompt:
# Story 1: One action bar for stories and enablers

- **Story**: XXX-document-action-bar
- **Created**: 2026-11-27
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: open a story with no diagram and see a bare Diagrams button; generate a sequence diagram, insert it and see its icon appear on
  the button; add a class diagram and see both; open an enabler and see only Sync, Save and Delete; edit, Save, and check that nothing
  reached GitHub.

## Story

As a team member, I want the same bar of actions on every story and enabler I open, and to see at a glance which diagrams a story already
has, so that I always find an action in the same place and do not generate a diagram that already exists.

## Acceptance tests

The bar of a story

- [ ] **Given** an open story, **Then** the bar shows, from left to right: "Add task", "Diagrams", "UI", "Sync", "Save", "Delete", then the
  close button.
- [ ] **Given** an open architectural enabler, **Then** the bar shows "Sync", "Save", "Delete" and the close button, in that order, and no
  Add task, Diagrams or UI.
- [ ] **Given** a story and an enabler, **Then** their Sync, Save and Delete buttons look and behave the same: same label, icon, size,
  colours, hints and keyboard focus.
- [ ] **Given** a driver or an ADR open in the builder, **Then** none of the six buttons shows (they are read-only here), only the close
  button.
- [ ] **Given** a narrow window, **Then** the buttons keep their order and wrap to a second line instead of being cut.

Diagrams that the story holds

- [ ] **Given** a story with no diagram, **Then** the Diagrams button shows its icon, "Diagrams" and the arrow, and nothing else.
- [ ] **Given** a story that holds a sequence diagram, **Then** the button also shows the sequence diagram icon, and its accessible name is
  "Diagrams: the story has a sequence diagram".
- [ ] **Given** a story that holds a class diagram, **Then** the button shows the class diagram icon, and its accessible name is "Diagrams:
  the story has a class diagram".
- [ ] **Given** a story that holds both, **Then** the button shows both icons, sequence first, and its accessible name is "Diagrams: the
  story has a sequence diagram and a class diagram".
- [ ] **Given** the button with a diagram icon, **When** the pointer rests on it, **Then** the hint names the diagrams it holds, for
  example "Sequence and class diagrams in the story".
- [ ] **Given** the menu is open, **Then** each kind the story holds has the chip "In the story" and the line "Open the diagram that the
  story holds.", and a kind it does not hold has its description, as today.
- [ ] **Given** the user inserts a diagram, **Then** its icon appears on the button at once. **Given** the user removes it, **Then** the
  icon goes at once.
- [ ] **Given** a diagram came down from GitHub (story 3), **Then** its icon shows on the button as soon as it is stored.
- [ ] **Given** a story that holds a UI example, **Then** the UI button keeps its green dot, as today.

Save stores, and only stores

- [ ] **Given** an open story or enabler, **When** the user presses Save or Ctrl+S in the text, **Then** the text is stored in the project's
  database, the sub-line says "Saved." for a moment, and no request is made to GitHub.
- [ ] **Given** the user changed a task, a link, a diagram, the UI example or Cross enabler, **Then** that is stored in the database as it
  is today, and no request is made to GitHub either.
- [ ] **Given** the document was saved and not synced, **Then** the Sync button has a dot and the hint "Saved here, not on GitHub yet.
  Sync to push it."
- [ ] **Given** unsaved changes in the text, **Then** Sync is disabled with the hint "Save the story first" (or "Save the enabler first"),
  as today.

## Business rules and constraints

- **One component.** The bar is one React component (in the spike, `DocumentActionBar`) used by the story and by the enabler. Which buttons
  show is decided by the kind of document, not by copies of the markup.
- **The order is fixed**: Add task, Diagrams, UI, Sync, Save, Delete. An enabler shows the last three of them.
- **The diagrams shown on the button are the ones stored with the story**, not a draft that is being generated and not yet inserted.
- **Save never talks to GitHub.** Only Sync pushes and Delete opens a pull request.

## Out of scope

- Diagrams, UI examples and tasks for an enabler.
- Other diagram kinds than sequence and class.
- A count of tasks on Add task.

## Tasks

- [ ] Extract the buttons of the header of `FileView` into a `DocumentActionBar` component with the kind, the sessions (tasks, diagrams,
  UI), the sync, Save and Delete as props, and the fixed order.
- [ ] Use it for the story (six buttons) and for the enabler (Sync, Save, Delete).
- [ ] Show on the Diagrams button the icon of each kind the story holds, with the accessible name and the hint.
- [ ] Add the dot and the hint "Saved here, not on GitHub yet" to Sync when the saved document differs from what was last synced.
- [ ] Test the buttons per kind, their order, and the diagram icons for none, one and both kinds.

tasks.text: Create the `DocumentActionBar` React component in the `ui` layer, accepting `kind`, `diagramsInStory`, `hasSavedUnsynced`, `hasUnsavedText`, and action callbacks as props (ADR-0007, AE-0002).
Render the six buttons for a story and the three buttons for an enabler in the fixed order, and render only the close button for drivers and ADRs.
Add the sequence-diagram and class-diagram icons to the Diagrams button when the corresponding diagrams are present in `diagramsInStory`, with the correct accessible name and tooltip.
Add the "saved but not synced" dot and tooltip to the Sync button, and disable Sync with its tooltip when `hasUnsavedText` is true.
Replace the existing header buttons in `FileView` with `DocumentActionBar` for both stories and enablers.

Write Jest tests covering: button set per document kind, fixed order, diagram icons for none / sequence only / class only / both, accessible names, Sync dot and disabled state, and immediate icon update on diagram insert and remove (Principle: UI/Front end Tests pay only for what they assert).
Verify the full build and test suite completes within the ten-minute budget (Practice: Ten-Minute Build).
